title: Data residency, ZDR, keys and private endpoints
summary: Four different controls that people mix up: where inference runs (residency), whether content is retained (ZDR and abuse monitoring), who holds the encryption key (customer-managed keys) and how traffic reaches the service (private networking).
useIf: A regulator, customer contract or data classification limits where prompts go, how long they persist, who can decrypt them or which network they cross.
avoidIf: You assume one control covers the others. Each answers a different question and each can disable features.

explain.caption: Name the question before choosing a control. Checked 2026-10-13.
head: Control
Question it answers
What it does not do
rows: Residency (deployment type)
Where does inference run and where is data at rest?

At rest data stays in the designated geography. Global types may run inference in any region, Data Zone types stay in the US, EU or APAC zone, Standard and Regional Provisioned types stay in the geography [[r24]]
Retention (ZDR, modified abuse monitoring)
Is content stored for abuse review or application state?
OpenAI keeps abuse-monitoring logs up to 30 days by default. ZDR and Modified Abuse Monitoring need approval. Some endpoints (threads, vector stores, fine-tuning jobs) are not ZDR eligible [[r25]]
Customer-managed key (CMK)
Who controls the key for data at rest?

Covers associated storage (project artifacts, uploaded files, evaluation data), not model inference. Uses Key Vault or Managed HSM, RSA 2048 bits or more. Grant the managed identity key access first, and omit `keyVersion` to follow the latest version. Some previews lack CMK [[r26]]
Private endpoint and VNet
Which network path does traffic take?
Some tools stay public or are unsupported under isolation [[r27]] [[r28]]

explain.md: **Residency.** Microsoft advises starting with Global Standard unless residency, reserved throughput or batch forces a change. Global Batch and Data Zone Batch give a 50% discount. The Developer tier is for fine-tuned model evaluation only, with a 24-hour lifetime and no SLA or residency guarantee [[r24]].

**Retention.** On Foundry, prompts and completions are not used to train base models. Stateful features (Responses API, threads, stored completions, files, vector stores) keep data at rest in your resource in the same geography, AES-256 encrypted, deletable. Abuse monitoring uses automated review by default with possible human review, and approved customers can get modified abuse monitoring that removes storage and human review [[r22]] [[r23]]. On OpenAI, under ZDR `store` on `/v1/responses` and `/v1/chat/completions` is always treated as false [[r25]]. Background mode keeps data for about 10 minutes, which conflicts with ZDR [[tr7]].

**Private networking.** Disable public network access and use a private endpoint, or allow selected networks. Agent Service setups are Basic, Standard (bring your own Storage, AI Search and Cosmos DB) and Standard with a bring-your-own VNet. Under isolation MCP, AI Search, Code Interpreter, function calling, OpenAPI, Azure Functions, A2A and file search work. Bing grounding, web search and SharePoint grounding use public endpoints. Browser automation, computer use, image generation and Logic Apps are not supported [[r27]] [[r28]].

explain.title: Zero retention does not mean nothing is stored
explain.md: Some endpoints are not ZDR eligible and keep state until you delete it. Some previews lack CMK. Check each feature you plan to use against the control you need.

whereToUse: Regulated workloads (health, finance, public sector) with data location rules
Contracts that forbid retention of prompts beyond the request
Environments with a key-ownership policy for data at rest
Enterprises that require private connectivity from a VNet to model and agent services
Architecture reviews that must map each requirement to a specific control

use: Choose the deployment type from the residency need: Data Zone or Regional before self-hosting
Request ZDR or modified abuse monitoring when content retention is the blocker
Add CMK when policy demands you control the key for stored artifacts
avoid: Assuming CMK protects inference, since it covers storage at rest only
Enabling private networking and then expecting browser automation or computer use to work
Using ZDR with features that need stored state or background mode
flips: Required tool is public-only (web search, Bing grounding): residency or isolation requirements may rule it out
Stateful feature needed (threads, vector stores): ZDR eligibility may block it
Volume and custom weights justify GPUs: self-hosting may deliver stricter control

pitfalls.symptom: Auditors find prompts outside the allowed region
pitfalls.cause: A Global deployment type was used where inference must stay in a zone
pitfalls.fix: Use Data Zone or Regional types, and verify the deployment type of every endpoint in code review.

pitfalls.symptom: Feature fails or silently stores state after ZDR is approved
pitfalls.cause: The endpoint is not ZDR eligible, or background mode keeps data for about 10 minutes
pitfalls.fix: Check per-endpoint eligibility, avoid ineligible endpoints and disable background mode for ZDR projects.

pitfalls.symptom: Agent tool works in dev but fails in the locked-down network
pitfalls.cause: Browser automation, computer use, image generation and Logic Apps are not supported under isolation
pitfalls.fix: Pick tools from the supported list or keep that tool in a separate, non-isolated environment.

scenarios.title: EU inference rule
scenarios.situation: A contract says personal data must be processed inside the EU. There is no rule about retention or key ownership. Load is moderate.
constraints: Inference must stay in the EU zone
unknowns: Is the needed model available as a Data Zone deployment?
scenarios.question: Which control do you reach for first?

options.name: Private endpoint only
options.why: It controls network path, not where inference runs, so processing could still happen outside the EU on a Global type.
options.tradeoff: Right when the requirement is that traffic never crosses the public internet.

options.name: Data Zone deployment for the EU
options.why: Data Zone types keep inference in the US, EU or APAC zone, which matches the rule.
options.tradeoff: Model and capacity availability may trail Global deployments.

options.name: Customer-managed key
options.why: CMK covers data at rest in associated storage, not inference location.
options.tradeoff: Right when policy demands you own the key for stored files and artifacts.

flips.then: Add ZDR or modified abuse monitoring and check endpoint eligibility.

flips.if: The model is not offered in the zone
flips.then: Consider a different model or self-hosting in an EU region.

scenarios.takeaway: Match the control to the question: residency answers 'where'.

scenarios.title: No retention, but needs agent state
scenarios.situation: A public-sector team is approved for zero data retention. They want an agent that keeps thread state and uses vector stores for documents.
unknowns: Can state live in your own storage?
scenarios.question: How do you reconcile ZDR with state?

options.name: Keep state in your own stores and use only ZDR-eligible endpoints
options.why: Threads and vector stores are not ZDR eligible, so you hold state yourself and keep control of retention.
options.tradeoff: You build and secure the state layer.

options.name: Use hosted threads and vector stores anyway
options.why: Those endpoints keep application state until deleted, which contradicts a no-retention intent.
options.tradeoff: Fine where retention in your resource, with deletion controls, is acceptable.

options.name: Turn on background mode for long runs
options.why: Background mode retains data for about 10 minutes, which conflicts with ZDR.
options.tradeoff: Use it where ZDR does not apply.

flips.if: Retention in your own resource with deletion is acceptable
flips.then: Foundry stateful features with CMK may be simpler.
Use synchronous calls, no background mode.

scenarios.takeaway: ZDR changes which features you can use. Check eligibility per endpoint.

scenarios.title: Private network and a web-research agent
scenarios.situation: A bank requires all AI traffic over private endpoints with public access disabled. A team wants an agent that browses the public web and uses computer use for a portal.
constraints: Agent needs web search and UI control
unknowns: Can browsing run in a separate environment?
Is an API available for the portal?
scenarios.question: What do you propose?

options.name: Keep the isolated agent on supported tools and run web and UI work in a separate sandbox with controlled egress
options.why: Computer use and browser automation are not supported under isolation and web search uses a public endpoint, so they need a different, controlled environment.
options.tradeoff: Two environments to build, secure and monitor.

options.name: Enable computer use inside the isolated project
options.why: It is not supported under network isolation.
options.tradeoff: Possible in a non-isolated project with a sandbox and confirmations.

options.name: Relax isolation for everything
options.tradeoff: Gives up the private-networking requirement for the whole agent.

flips.if: The portal offers an API or MCP server
flips.then: Use it inside the isolated setup and skip computer use.

flips.if: Web research can use an internal indexed corpus
flips.then: Use AI Search or file search, which work under isolation.

scenarios.takeaway: Private networking is a tool filter. Map each tool to the isolation rules.

quiz.q: Match each control to the question it answers.

pairs.r: Is content stored beyond the request?
Who controls the key for stored data?

quiz.explain: Each control answers a different question, so one does not substitute for another. CMK covers storage at rest, not inference, and private endpoints do not set where inference runs.

quiz.q: Which tools are unsupported under Foundry network isolation as of 2026-10-13?
quiz.explain: Browser automation, computer use, image generation and Logic Apps are not supported under isolation. AI Search and file search are supported.

quiz.q: What does a customer-managed key in Foundry protect?
options: Data at rest in associated storage
Model inference in memory while a request runs
quiz.explain: CMK covers data at rest in the resource's associated storage, such as project artifacts, uploaded files and evaluation data. It does not cover inference, network path or location.

flashcards.front: Which Foundry deployment types keep inference inside a zone or geography?
flashcards.back: Data Zone types stay in the US, EU or APAC zone. Standard and Regional Provisioned stay in the geography. Global types may run in any region.

flashcards.front: What does OpenAI ZDR do to `store`?
flashcards.back: Under ZDR, `store` on `/v1/responses` and `/v1/chat/completions` is always treated as false. Some endpoints are not eligible.

flashcards.front: Name two tools that fail under Foundry network isolation.
flashcards.back: Browser automation and computer use. Image generation and Logic Apps are also unsupported. Bing grounding, web search and SharePoint grounding use public endpoints.
